title: Fidelity-aware Headroom Allocator and Tenant Quarantine Guidelines (PRD sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a fidelity-aware headroom allocator that proactively reserves soft-capacity for different tenant fidelity tiers and an associated tenant quarantine (soft-eviction) guideline. Goal: reduce tail latency spikes and emergency preemptions during microbursts while preserving predictable economics for committed tenants.

Context / problem statement:
- Dedicated pools experience short, high-intensity bursts from a small number of tenants and sustained load changes from others.
- Existing autoscalers react to metrics and either scale slowly (cold start pain) or trigger bulk preemptions / hard-evictions with poor customer experience.
- We need a mechanism to: (1) keep short-term latency SLOs for high-fidelity tenants, (2) let opportunistic tenants consume leftover capacity, and (3) gracefully quarantine noisy tenants when oversubscription threatens SLOs.

High-level proposal:
1) Fidelity-aware headroom allocator (FAHA)
   - Maintain three fidelity bands per pool: High (latency-sensitive, SLA-backed), Medium (best-effort, billed reserved), Opportunistic (burstable / cheaper).
   - For each band compute real-time headroom budget H_t = base_headroom + burst_delta * burst_score + model_fingerprint_factor.
   - Headroom is applied as pre-warmed GPU slots or soft-affinity tokens that avoid cold-start overhead for high-fidelity lanes.

2) Tenant quarantine and soft-eviction guidelines
   - Quarantine = transient restriction that moves tenant traffic into degraded lanes (reduced concurrency, forced batching, or model-fidelity downgrade) for a configurable window before any hard eviction.
   - Quarantine triggers: sustained tail latency > 99.9th SLO, sudden delta in token/sec vs forecast > x%, or KV cache pressure > threshold.
   - Quarantine outcomes: automatic recovery (if behavior normalizes), scheduled remediation notification to tenant, or escalate to hard eviction if repeated offenses.

Why different from existing approaches:
- Instead of binary reserved vs spot, FAHA ties headroom to observed workload fidelity and model sensitivity.
- Quarantine is a graduated control that preserves product availability while enforcing fairness and protecting SLOs.

User stories:
- As an enterprise product owner (High), I want predictable low tail latency even during noisy neighbor bursts so my customer-facing features stay within SLA.
- As a growth company (Opportunistic), I want cheap burst access with clear fallbacks and transparent signals when I'm being throttled/quarantined.
- As an SRE, I want a deterministic set of runbook steps and telemetry so we can diagnose and roll back quarantine decisions.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Tail latency (99.9th) for High fidelity tenants: reduce emergency preemptions by >= 80% over historical baseline in pilot pools.
- Opportunistic tenant satisfaction: measured by success rate of burst requests (Tokens accepted vs rejected) — target >= 70% for typical microbursts.
- Operational: mean time to detect and quarantine noisy tenant < 60s; mean time to resolve false-positive quarantine < 10min.

Design details:
- Signals used by FAHA:
  * Per-tenant token/sec and request concurrency
  * 99th/99.9th latency percentiles (per-model, per-route)
  * KV cache hit ratio and memory pressure
  * Forecast deviation signal (compare short-window rate against rolling forecast)
  * Model_fingerprint: an embedding of model family + sequence length distribution used to bias headroom allocation (models with long-seq cost more).

- Headroom computation (rough formula):
  H_t = clip(H_base + alpha * burst_score + beta * model_seq_penalty, min_H, pool_max)
  where burst_score = sigmoid((r_now - forecast)/forecast_window) * burst_weight

- Allocation semantics:
  * Headroom slots are soft-reserved: they are prioritized for High fidelity but can be borrowed by Opportunistic with a reclaim TTL.
  * Borrowing imposes a reclaimable label; the runtime supports immediate preemption within reclaim TTL by lowering priority and triggering graceful checkpointing/partial response where supported.

Quarantine control knobs (configurable per-pool):
- quarantine_window_seconds (default 300s)
- throttle_concurrency_pct (default 50%)
- batch_enforcement_threshold (force batching for quarantined tenants)
- model_fidelity_swap (allow automatic switch to quantized model if candidate available)
- notification_policy (email + console + webhook)

APIs / UX sketches:
- Admin API (product team / tenant-facing console):
  POST /pools/{pool_id}/headroom/config -> set base_headroom, fidelity_band_weights
  GET /pools/{pool_id}/headroom -> current allocations per band
  POST /tenants/{tenant_id}/quarantine -> manual quarantine (ops)
  GET /tenants/{tenant_id}/quarantine -> status, history, ETA

- Tenant-facing signals: in-console indicator, webhook with reason code, and a short-lived claim-check indicating expected duration and actions they can take (reduce batch sizes, lower fidelity).

Operational runbook (on-call):
- Detection -> automated quarantine triggered -> page SRE for repeated >2 quarenstines in 24h -> run diag flow: check model fingerprint, check recent deploys, check traffic pattern (spikes from single IP / sudden seq length change) -> either allow auto-recovery or escalate to manual mitigation (temporary hard eviction).
- Rollback path: restore previous headroom config and release quarantined tenants.

Compatibility and edge cases:
- Multi-pool tenants: headroom decisions are pool-local; for multi-pool tenancy we include a cross-pool coordinator that honors tenant-level SLAs and balances headroom tokens.
- Model variants: if downgraded model lacks feature parity, outbound notification must include degradation notice; we avoid auto-swap for models that affect correctness-sensitive tasks.
- Billing implications: opportunistic borrowing tracked and surfaced as burst credits consumed; prolonged quarantine periods trigger customer support outreach and potential billing adjustments.

Monitoring and telemetry:
- Dashboards: per-pool headroom utilization, per-band latency SLOs, quarantine state timeline, false-positive rate for quarantines.
- Alerts: pool headroom exhausted for >2min, quarantine count > threshold, repeated quarantine for single tenant >3 times/day.

Pilot plan:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): offline simulation on last 30 days of telemetry using historic traces to tune alpha/beta.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): deploy FAHA in pilot pool (us-west-2 small dedicated pool) with opportunistic enabled and quarantine acts as opt-in (no auto-hard-evict).
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): enable quarantine auto-window and SRE-runbook; measure metrics; iterate.
- Phase 3: gradual ramp across fleets with per-region tuning.

Open questions / risks:
- How to choose thresholds to minimize false-positive quarantines? (need A/B trials and telemetry-driven thresholds)
- How to surface headroom economics to sales/finance so pricing for burst credits remains simple and defensible?
- Interactions with existing reserved + burst credit systems — avoid double-accounting for headroom.

Implementation notes (engineering TODOs):
- Autoscaler hooks: expose real-time headroom token pool and APIs for immediate reclaim. (ENG: autoscaler team)
- Runtime support: tagging work items with reclaimable priority and fast preempt path (SERVING-RUNTIME)
- Console: tenant view + per-pool controls + notification pipeline (CONSOLE)

References / related docs:
- linked artifacts listed in metadata.
- See also: previous warm-pool and burst-credit drafts for overlap; this doc focuses on fidelity-aware allocation and graduated quarantine as softer control.

Next steps:
- Align with autoscaler and serving runtime owners for an interface contract by 2025-02-10.
- Prepare simulation harness (owner: Diego) to test on Dec/Jan traces and produce recommended alpha/beta = preliminary values.
- Schedule pilot rollout with SRE window and on-call runbook run-through.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough; please highlight obvious missing safety checks and billing interactions.
- I expect we will iterate the headroom formula after simulations; focus review on the quarantine semantics and operational safety.
